implementation_notes: System.Threading.Channels is the in-box realization (part of the shared framework since .NET Core 3.0): Channel.CreateBounded/Unbounded yields a ChannelReader and ChannelWriter, BoundedChannelOptions controls capacity and overflow, and SingleReader promises a single consumer so the implementation can skip multi-reader synchronization; ChannelReader.ReadAllAsync gives the consumer an awaitable loop in place of the classic blocking take. The brokered form (Azure Service Bus, MSMQ, RabbitMQ) is required when the channel must outlive the process, and BlockingCollection<T> over ConcurrentQueue<T> remains the synchronous fallback without the package.
pitfalls: SingleReader/SingleWriter are declarations the creator makes to the implementation, not runtime enforcement; breaking the promise can silently disable the single-reader fast path.
A bounded channel parks WriteAsync when full (FullMode.Wait is the default) - overload blocks producers instead of dropping, which must be intended.
Readers wait forever if the writer never calls Complete(); a forgotten completion looks like a hung service, not an exception.
